
### Interrupts for the notes of the Unit 3 - Architecture of 8086 microprocessor: register organization, bus interface unit, execution unit, memory addressing, and memory segmentation. Operating modes. Instruction sets, instruction format, Types of instructions. Interrupts: hardware and software interrupts. in the subject of Microprocessor KCS

* Interrupts are signals that are sent to the processor to indicate the occurrence of an event.
* Hardware interrupts are generated by external devices such as keyboards, mice, and printers.
* Software interrupts are generated by the processor itself, either in response to an instruction or as a result of an exception or error.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports two types of interrupts: hardware interrupts and software interrupts.
* The 8086 microprocessor has a 16-bit register called the interrupt vector table (IVT) which contains the addresses of the interrupt service routines (ISRs) for each type of interrupt.
* The 8086 microprocessor also has a 16-bit register called the interrupt mask register (IMR) which is used to enable or disable specific interrupts.
* The 8086 microprocessor has a bus interface unit (BIU) which is responsible for managing the data and address buses.
* The 8086 microprocessor has an execution unit (EU) which is responsible for decoding instructions and executing them.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports two types of memory addressing: real-mode addressing and protected-mode addressing.
* Real-mode addressing is used in the 8086 microprocessor to access memory located in the first 1MB of RAM.
* Protected-mode addressing is used in the 8086 microprocessor to access memory located beyond the first 1MB of RAM.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports memory segmentation which allows it to access memory beyond the first 1MB of RAM.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports two instruction sets: the 8086 instruction set and the 80286 instruction set.
* The 8086 instruction set consists of 8-bit and 16-bit instructions, while the 80286 instruction set consists of 32-bit instructions.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports two types of instructions: privileged instructions and non-privileged instructions.
* Privileged instructions can only be executed when the processor is in privileged mode while non-privileged instructions can be executed in any mode.
* The 8086 microprocessor supports two types of interrupts: hardware interrupts and software interrupts.
* Hardware interrupts are generated by external devices such as keyboards, mice, and printers.
* Software interrupts are generated by the processor itself, either in response to an instruction or as a result of an exception or error.
* Hardware interrupts are serviced by interrupt service routines (ISRs) located in the interrupt vector table (IVT).
* Software interrupts are serviced by interrupt service routines (ISRs) located in the interrupt vector table (IVT) or in the interrupt vector table extension (IVTE).
* The interrupt mask register (IMR) is used to enable or disable specific interrupts.
